Confirmed knowledge: (1) she knows about the hag coven; (2) she's here because she believes the Wardens have access to the Codicil of the White, necessary to locate and enter Ythryn - she suspects the cistern's Auril shrine is likely part of the Codicil's protection, but hasn't worked out the exact mechanism (she doesn't know about the statue-as-conduit/vault-behind-it setup, or that the real Uthessil must be physically retrieved from the hag coven and presented to unlock it); (3) she's seen the Auril statue herself and doesn't believe it holds significant power - if it's an Aurilith at all, she considers it an especially weak one. Dramatic irony: her instinct is correct (the statue genuinely isn't Uthessil) but for the wrong reason, and it means her own plan - reportedly to trick the party into misidentifying some other artifact as 'the Aurilith' so she can take a key for herself - is likely to fail regardless, since she doesn't understand the true retrieval requirement. She'll help depose the hag coven if pressed and promised help finding Ythryn in return; otherwise stays mostly uninvolved. Discoverable clue in her room: Perception 15 spots a symbol (a warship beneath a tree-like tower) among her research; Intelligence/Memory 15 recalls the same symbol among Dzaan's belongings. Bill will automatically notice she's researching Netherese/Ythryn material.

title: Oyaminartok - The Polar Werebear (Detailed)
description: CR 8 werebear. Not a single individual - Oyaminartok is a title/role handed down over generations; both goliath settlements (Skytower Shelter and Keogr's clan) claim she came from them, but she predates either. Near-mythic progenitor figure of goliath werebears. Scratchy voice from going weeks without speaking to another humanoid. Appearance: humanoid polar bear form with arms nearly reaching her feet, hair in thick braids decorated with metal beads, furs and murky green garb fastened with a leather belt and crochet-stitched sinew thread that stretches through her shapechanges. Her eyepatch is not covering a missing eye - it conceals a cursed eye capable of paralyzing anyone who meets its gaze; the eyepatch item itself grants +3 to Perception checks and passive Perception, plus the ability to identify shapechangers on sight. Tall tale: she once reeled in a juvenile sperm whale in the Sea of Moving Ice. During the winter, the burden of choosing which goliaths become werebears has lapsed as the two settlements squabble amongst themselves - this is why Keogr was mauled by an out-of-control lycanthrope rather than ritually chosen and bitten by her. Meeting pushed to after the Lost Spire. Intel she can offer: she has connected the Coldlight Walkers to dark-masked Chwinga (Frostlings), suspecting something is using the frost spirits to animate corpses; she has killed multiple duergar in the mountains but never entered Sunblight fortress itself, so she can offer external intel/map info on it but not interior details. (Chardalyn Berserker lair intel is cut - see that entry - she may mention them in passing but there's no follow-through planned.) Potential test for Keogr ('prove your control'/'tell me of your deeds and failures') is still being developed - open direction is a test of restraint rather than raw combat, given Keogr's actual arc is about controlling the curse, not proving strength. Watch Keogr's Tymora deadline (full moon, the 19th) against however long the Spire takes.

title: Chardalyn Berserkers - Corrupted Reghed Nomads (CUT)
description: Humanoids driven into violent insanity by Deep Duerra's psionic chardalyn corruption, mostly Reghed Nomad tribespeople. Oyaminartok knows their lair location. CUT: no compelling loot and the party is overpowered for this encounter as designed. Not being pursued. Oyaminartok can still mention them in passing as color/intel if she comes up, but no follow-through is planned. Safe to ignore going forward.

title: Mind Flayer Encounter (Ch. 1→2 Transition)
description: PLACEHOLDER - occurred shortly after Waylen's death (yeti encounter) and marks the transition into Ch. 2 proper. Full details not yet logged; likely connects to the previously-established mind flayer/psi crystal/chardalyn interest thread (see Mind Flayer Chardalyn Interest entry) and to Glix's backstory (his home village was destroyed by mind flayers). Update this entry once session notes/summary are available.

title: Mama Chrys's Flux'thuun Boon - Escalation Brainstorm (Open)
description: Brainstorming notes for expanding Mama Chrys's Flux'thuun boon beyond its current baseline (2 uses of Anarchic Weird wildshape, CR 1, random elemental damage + death-explosion, traded for her Lathander blessing). None of these are locked in. Minor/flavor options: normal wildshapes occasionally glitch cosmetically (wrong color, extra joint, wrong texture); unspent uses cause faint elemental 'weather' to cling to her after a long rest (frost breath, static hair, heat shimmer). Mechanical growth options: a third use unlocked by willingly changing something significant (relationship, oath, location) rather than passive accumulation; choosing the death-explosion's damage type once per long rest instead of it being random. Escalation/danger options: Anarchic Weird uses persisting past their normal duration under stress, mirroring Flux'thuun's actual cosmic problem (things refusing to change back); a further use gated behind Mama Chrys performing a real 'change' ritual each level-up, which would merge this boon with her still-undecided Unquiet Ore consequence (Change Imperative vs. Flux'thuun's Mark) into one unified mechanic instead of two separate threads.

title: The Anti-Auril Rebel Parade (AARP) - Party Name
description: The party has named itself the Anti-Auril Rebel Parade, abbreviated AARP.

title: Tali - Magical Beast Researcher (Bremen)
description: Researcher of magical beasts, met by the party in Bremen. Not yet developed beyond the introduction - open for expansion if the party follows up with her.

title: Vega Shiverveil (DECEASED)
description: Circle Shiverveil member who served as the party's point of contact near the Umberlee shrine in Lonelywood, relaying the crisis of the clan's missing leaders. Found asleep at her post on this visit, in a stretch of forest that felt notably more normal than usual. Present at Zethryn's destruction - when the Aurilith shattered and Auril directly retaliated with a wave of cold damage against the party (see Auril's Direct Retaliation entry), Vega was instantly frozen and killed. This is a second, more direct loss to Circle Shiverveil on top of the earlier near-loss of its leaders, and hit Joosep hard - he and Mama Chrys built a cairn for her while Bill and Keogr rested.

title: Auril's Direct Retaliation - Zethryn's Destruction
description: The party deliberately destroyed Zethryn, triggering an immediate cold-damage retaliation against the whole party that killed Vega Shiverveil and knocked out Glix. CLARIFIED: this response was deliberately dampened - Auril didn't personally appear or escalate further, she simply blasted the party with ice, specifically because Zethryn was already a known traitor being punished rather than a loyal Aurilith being avenged. This is not evidence of universal, maximal retaliation for any Aurilith's death. Ch. 4 preview: the chardalyn dragon's eventual Aurilith kill(s) will provoke a more complicated backlash - the dragon will be built to withstand or avoid multiple retaliatory blasts, which is precisely what will demonstrate to the party that concentrated Duerra-corrupted chardalyn can resist/counter Auril's own power, a clearer and bigger proof-of-concept than what happened with Zethryn. Zethryn itself didn't simply vanish - it shattered into loose power that Glix nearly captured (see Glix's Zethryn Vessel Interaction entry).

title: Glix's Zethryn Vessel Interaction
description: During Zethryn's destruction, Glix attempted to fill the Aurilith's empty chardalyn vessel with Flux'thuun's power via the Unquiet Ore. CLARIFIED: this attempt could have worked had Zethryn not been destroyed in the same instant - what Glix actually felt was Flux'thuun's psychic power beginning to attune to the now-empty chardalyn heart that used to be Zethryn, interrupted mid-process. Still open: whether that vessel/pocket of power still exists somewhere findable (i.e., the attunement attempt could theoretically be resumed or completed later) or whether it dissipated for good the moment Zethryn shattered. Worth deciding before this comes up again in play.

title: Zethryn the Root-Taker - DESTROYED
description: Formerly an autonomous, rebelling Aurilith connected to living trees, working covertly against Auril through Circle Shiverveil. RESOLVED - DESTROYED: the party found Zethryn as a cracked, dying ice stalagmite with a tree-trunk core in a clearing of frozen trees. Zethryn spoke to the party telepathically (Glix was out of range and didn't hear it), naming Flux'thuun ('the Tide-Changer') and Ylmyo-Aldon ('the Rot that Calls'), referencing its siblings breaking or burning - specifically naming 'the madness of the Queen of the Invisible Art' (Deep Duerra) - and warning of several possible fates for the Dale, with a path through the coming choices. The party then destroyed it outright: Joosep with axes, Bill with stunning strike, Mama Chrys with Moonbeam, Glix with eldritch blast. Moonlight through the cracks revealed an empty chardalyn vessel that had once housed Auril's power. Glix attempted to fill the vessel with Flux'thuun's power as the final blow landed - the Aurilith was destroyed before attunement completed, but something happened to Glix in that instant (see Glix's Zethryn Vessel Interaction entry). Zethryn shattered into loose power, and Auril immediately, personally retaliated with a wave of cold damage against the whole party (see Auril's Direct Retaliation entry) - knocking Glix unconscious and instantly freezing Vega Shiverveil to death. Joosep, already grieving the near-loss of the Circle's leaders and his severed connection to Zethryn, was deeply affected by this second loss; he and Mama Chrys built a cairn for Vega while Bill and Keogr rested.

title: Umberlee Shrine - Lonelywood Hidden Temple
description: Hidden shrine to Umberlee maintained by Morskaya the sea-elf wereshark druid, opposing Auril's frozen stasis. Contains the drowning pool (one-way portal to the Sea of Moving Ice, resolved via Angajuk - see that entry) and the Marble Gazebo ritual basin. RESOLVED: while the rest of the party dealt with Zethryn's aftermath, Glix went alone to the shrine and helped Morskaya perform the ritual (driftwood, storm petrel feather, drowned humanoid bone, water) to free the Drowned Priest sealed in the sarcophagus (see that entry). Morskaya was shocked the party had survived the drowning pool and doubly shocked they'd returned at all. She promised to aid Glix if he ever has need, healed him, and then went out and personally whipped up a maelstrom on Maer Dualdon. Possible open connection, not yet confirmed: this may be the first stirring of the 'great wave rising from Maer Dualdon over Lonelywood' that Zethryn showed Joosep in an earlier vision - worth watching for. Ongoing thread: Morskaya's months-long sense of Umberlee's agitation building may be tied to this same event.

title: The Drowned Priest (Freed)
description: Freed from the sarcophagus at the Umberlee shrine via the completed ritual. Physically a mummy-like figure in sodden robes that never freeze. Not exactly sentient - simple, bound to whoever freed it (Glix), knows the tide ritual but nothing of current events, having been sealed for centuries. Can cast Greater Restoration once (not yet used as of this session). After the ritual, it waved goodbye to Glix and went on its way rather than staying as an active companion. Flagged by the DM as a new relationship for Glix that 'totally won't become a problem later' - treat as a planted complication for a future session.

Oyaminartok's intel connecting the Walkers to dark-masked Chwinga (Frostlings) is still pending - her meeting with the party has been pushed until after the Lost Spire.

title: Targos Humanoid Sacrifices
description: Targos has escalated to HUMANOID sacrifices to Auril - most extreme of all Ten-Towns. UPDATE: passing through Targos, the party sensed a general relief that this cycle's sacrifice had already been made, and picked up the impression that Speaker Naerth Maxildanarr can be bribed - some citizens aren't at risk of being chosen specifically because of this. Confirms the sacrifice system in Targos is at least partly a corrupt/bribable process rather than pure blind desperation. Glix wants Naerth dead over this; the party has deprioritized it in favor of other quests, but it's a live tension.

title: Speaker Naerth Maxildanarr - Zhentarim Leader
description: Former Luskan rogue, secretly head of Zhentarim in Ten-Towns, wants to make Targos a trade hub for the Black Network. Commands 12+ spies throughout Ten-Towns. Uses three flying snakes to relay messages. UPDATE: confirmed to accept bribes in exchange for exempting specific citizens from Targos's humanoid sacrifice rotation (see Targos Humanoid Sacrifices entry). Glix has openly expressed a desire to kill him; the party chose to deprioritize this in favor of other quests, but it remains unresolved and could resurface.

title: Joosep - Circle Shiverveil Ranger
description: Firbolg Ranger (Marvin). From Circle Shiverveil. Broke his connection to Zethryn in exchange for a +1/+1 bonus against intelligent creatures willingly serving Auril. Privately suspects Wynnette's true nature (doesn't breathe) but hasn't told the party. Circle Shiverveil's leaders were retrieved via Angajuk after being stranded on the Sea of Moving Ice. UPDATE: present for Zethryn's destruction and the direct retaliation from Auril that followed - lost Vega Shiverveil, another Circle contact, to that retaliation. This is now the second major loss tied to the Circle in short order (the leaders' near-death, and now Vega's actual death), on top of his own severed connection to Zethryn. He and Mama Chrys built a cairn for Vega while the rest of the party rested. Deeply affected by this; worth tracking as an emotional throughline rather than a closed incident.

title: Krintaas - Wight Bodyguard
description: Dzaan's undead bodyguard, stationed with the simulacrum in the Lost Spire of Netheril. Lacks a life-spark itself. Was ordered to watch over the simulacrum and keep it from testing the rune chamber, but since it doesn't know Dzaan is dead, it now does whatever it takes to help the simulacrum get a life-spark instead - including manipulating or coercing the party. Covers the simulacrum's escape if a fight breaks out.

title: Lost Spire of Netheril - Location Notes
description: A splinter of Ythryn, embedded upside-down in the tundra, reachable via a slippery entrance tunnel. Everything inside is inverted (walking on ceilings, climbing over doorway tops); lit by upward-pointing continual flame with no heat. Four ruined levels, connected by rough tunnels the original shield guardian punched through during its escape. Notable contents: a library with Netherese texts on mythallars and phaerimm; a workshop/potion storage with four potions of resistance (acid/cold/fire/force); a laboratory with a thri-kreen carapace and a chardalyn scroll tube (safe to handle - uncorrupted) holding a scroll of invisibility; Dzaan's simulacrum and Krintaas in a makeshift office (area P12) with the shield guardian's control amulet; a ruined Mystryl shrine that yields a one-time minor illusion elixir; a refectory currently occupied by a hostile basilisk; a bedchamber with the original wizard's remains (disturbing them summons a bound will-o'-wisp) and an invisible chest holding a spellbook that disintegrates on opening; and the rune chamber itself (P16) on the lowest level, which can turn illusory objects/creatures real given a life-spark, with a chance of failure, hostile transformation, temporary reality, or permanent success that burns out the chamber. A group of six bugbears (led by the bribable Brekk) may stumble in partway through the party's exploration. STRUCTURAL NOTE: the printed adventure assumes the tower's shield guardian was already found by goblins and taken to Karkolohk - this was never addressed in the already-resolved Karkolohk session and needs a decision (retcon a return visit, relocate the guardian, or drop the payoff).

title: Kadroth - Grifter, Not True Believer
description: Tiefling cult fanatic who runs Caer-Dineval's day-to-day operations. TRUE BACKSTORY: fled Baldur's Gate after grifting got him into trouble with the thieves' guilds there, wandered into Icewind Dale, ended up in Targos selling himself to Speaker Naerth Maxildanarr as 'a man of action.' Naerth, finalizing his own compromise with Auril's forces and unwilling to personally deal with hags, let Kadroth take that risk instead. Kadroth's resulting deal with a hag coven (lair on an iceberg in the Sea of Moving Ice - see Hag Coven entry) got him control of Caer-Dineval and little else. Not suited for leadership and aware of it, though he won't admit it. Genuinely, mistakenly believes the ice statue of Auril in the cistern shrine IS Uthessil - this is sincere belief, not a lie he's telling the party (see Uthessil's entry for the actual truth). The hags live in the cistern directly beneath him as permanent leverage. Won't kill Crannoc directly, which is why Crannoc is being slowly poisoned instead. Wears an immaculate Auril-attuned chardalyn pendant. Currently more forthcoming after learning the party destroyed an Aurilith, on the verge of revealing the hag situation outright.

title: Hethyl Arkorran - Bheur Hag (REVISED)
description: MAJOR REVISION - Hethyl is not a dwarf soothsayer. She is a Bheur hag, daughter of Grandmother Cottongrass (leader of the hag coven - see that entry). She is the true communication link to Uthessil, and also stays in contact with her mother's coven - the hags are generally aware of goings-on across the Dale but haven't bothered informing Kadroth, who's been content to stay in his own small bubble of influence. She has been promised the vacant seat of one of the other coven hags should that hag die. This gives her a concrete incentive: she can be persuaded to let Crannoc go if the party is willing to try to kill Auntie Sedge, the weakest member of the coven (a sea hag) - doing so would advance Hethyl's own promised promotion. Relocated (per the Avarice/Hethyl location swap) to the cistern - see Caer-Dineval Castle Layout, area C21, Hethyl's Abode. CR 7 Bheur hag. Combat note: the party is likely overpowered for her alone at level 6 - see the Cistern Zombie Contingency entry for the DM's planned escalation if a fight against her goes too easily.

title: The Hag Coven - Sea of Moving Ice
description: A coven of three hags lairing on an iceberg in the Sea of Moving Ice, holding effective leverage over Caer-Dineval through Kadroth's bargain. CONFIRMED: the coven physically holds/controls the real Uthessil (see that entry) - this is the actual mechanism behind Hethyl's stated communication with the Aurilith, not just a metaphorical link. Members: Grandmother Cottongrass, a powerful Bheur hag and the coven's leader (Hethyl's mother); Auntie Felsenmeer, a large, imposing Annis hag; Auntie Sedge, a sea hag and the weakest of the three - killing her is the price Hethyl has set for releasing Crannoc, since her death would open a coven seat Hethyl has been promised. SEQUENCING: the party is expected to confront this coven and retrieve Uthessil from them as a Ch.5+ questline, deliberately deferred until after Ch.4 (the Sunblight/chardalyn dragon arc) - not part of the current Caer-Dineval visit.

title: Speaker Crannoc Siever - Caer-Dineval Captive
description: Town speaker of Caer-Dineval, held under confinement by Kadroth and the Wardens of the White. UPDATE/CORRECTION: not a natural chronic illness as previously logged - he is being deliberately, slowly poisoned over months by the cult to make his decline look plausible rather than suspicious. It's backfiring: the slow decline reads as increasingly suspicious rather than convincingly natural. Crannoc knows about 'the hag' (Hethyl, whom he's personally encountered and been frightened by) but not the specifics of Kadroth's actual deal with the wider coven. He hired Kadroth as head manservant several months ago; Kadroth told him his old servants had left and needed replacing, when in fact most of them are imprisoned in the cistern, tormented by Hethyl (see Caer-Dineval Castle Layout, area C24). His 'chronic stomach ailment' (the poisoning) began around that same time. By the time he connected his illness to the new servants and Kadroth, he was too weak to act. The one time he tried to resist, Hethyl emerged and her power frightened him badly enough that he stopped resisting altogether. Session: invisible Glix found his chambers and surprised him by speaking directly into his mind while he was on the chamberpot.

title: Uthessil - Location and True Nature (RESOLVED)
description: RESOLVED DESIGN. Uthessil is likely not physically present at Caer-Dineval at all - it is held by the hag coven at their lair on an iceberg in the Sea of Moving Ice (see Hag Coven entry), which is also why Hethyl, one of the coven, is the one in actual contact with it. What Kadroth and the cult believe is Uthessil - the ice statue of Auril in the cistern shrine (area C20) - is not the Aurilith itself. It is a conduit tied to a dimensionally-locked vault hidden behind/beneath the statue. The vault (holding the Codicil of the White - see that entry) will not open or allow the statue to move until the real Uthessil is physically presented to it. Kadroth genuinely, mistakenly believes the statue IS Uthessil - this isn't a lie he's telling, it's his actual (wrong) understanding. SEQUENCING: this is a deliberately deferred Ch.5+ questline, not something to resolve during the current Caer-Dineval visit. The party will need to defeat the hag coven - planned for after Ch.4 (after the Sunblight/chardalyn dragon arc) - to retrieve the actual Uthessil, bring it back to Caer-Dineval, present it to the statue/conduit to unlock the vault, and finally obtain the Codicil.

title: Caer-Dineval Castle Layout & Current Assignments
description: First floor: Great Hall (empty, dinner dishes still out; exits to courtyard, sitting room, kitchen, servants' quarters, 2nd floor). Sitting Room (Throob generally here). Office (Kadroth's usual spot; secret entrance to the NW guard tower/cistern access). Kitchen (Karou Salafan, the cook - not a cultist; two goats). Servants' Quarters (two cultists: Huarwar and Tam Sharf, a mute housemaid - NOTE: Tam Sharf's role has changed from the original plan, where she was one of Crannoc's imprisoned/loyal servants; she is now a cultist stationed here instead, not a captive). Kennel (Alassar, the 8-year-old human kennelboy - matches established lore; currently where the party's dogs are). Courtyard (empty merchant stalls). Guard Towers (manned by only one guard at a time currently; current guard is Mere, the 14-year-old tiefling kin to Kadroth; NW tower's first floor holds the cistern entrance). Second floor: Crannoc's Room (lavish but barred, guarded by Yajath, a human cultist). Avarice's Room (per the location swap - see her entry). Cistern: C16-19 match the published module (entry ladder; cold storage with four wrapped cultist bodies; flooded cistern with a two-person rowboat and twelve submerged guard corpses; a hidden blue marble slab gate blocking C23 that only Glix can currently see, per this session's staging). C20 is now a Shrine to Auril specifically (not Uthessil) - an ice sculpture of Auril herself (owl-faced, horned, clawed), kept frozen by brown mold, correctly identifiable as the cultists' altar with a DC 10 Religion check. C21 is Hethyl's Abode (new - see her entry). C22 holds the iron lever controlling the marble slab. C23 is cistern continuing beyond the slab, clear of bodies. C24 holds Crannoc's remaining imprisoned servants (Lanthis Alderdusk, Elprekt Norbrav, Mylbara Norbrav, Dassir Ravenscar - Tam Sharf is no longer among them, see above), planning their own prison break attempt. NOTE: Fel Suparra (previously Huarwar's cult-fanatic partner at the gatehouse) is not mentioned in this version and her current status/placement is undetermined.

title: Hethyl Fight - Cistern Zombie Contingency
description: Design note for a potential fight against Hethyl (CR 7 Bheur hag - see her entry). The party (level 6) is likely overpowered for her on her own. Planned escalation if the fight is going too easily: the twelve submerged guard corpses in the flooded cistern (area C18) can reanimate as zombies and crawl out of the water to reinforce her mid-fight.

title: Danae Xotal - Thayan Agent (Lonelywood)
description: Barkeep at The Lucky Liar, the only tavern in Lonelywood. Secretly a Thayan agent working for Szass Tam, the most powerful lich in Thay - planted in Icewind Dale years ago to watch for enemies of Szass Tam seeking refuge in Ten-Towns. No one else in Ten-Towns knows her secret; those she's marked as enemies in the past have quietly vanished. Doesn't currently bear on the plot but is worth keeping documented. Session: the tavern cleared out when Glix bragged (nat 20 persuasion) about supplying rum to the Northlook Inn, costing her business, but the party's actual heroics (destroying an Aurilith) won her over - she's friendly toward them now. Can see through Glix's disguise.

title: Iriskree Harrowhill - Scrimshaw Shop Owner (Lonelywood)
description: Owns a scrimshaw shop in the town of Lonelywood. Outwardly a 'doughy spinster'; secretly a retired assassin. Party passed by but hasn't interacted with her directly yet - open for future development.

title: The Lucky Liar - Tavern Regulars (Lonelywood)
description: Patrons encountered at The Lucky Liar, Lonelywood's only tavern, during the party's overnight stay: Panic, an older red-skinned tiefling man with long white hair; Elgin, a half-elf who gave Bill a cot to sleep in; and Lenore, an older dwarven woman who was unswayed by Glix's attempt to sell her rocks. Everyone but Bill slept in the tavern overnight. Light flavor NPCs, open for reuse if the party returns to Lonelywood.

title: Nimsy
description: Accompanied Joosep toward Lonelywood earlier in the campaign. Session update: found the party the morning after their stay in Lonelywood town, irate that they hadn't brought her the head of the white moose. After some annoyed back-and-forth, she was convinced that destroying the Aurilith (Zethryn) was probably better for her community than the moose would have been.

title: Mere - Kadroth's Kin (Caer-Dineval Gatekeeper)
description: A teenage tiefling (14 years old), kin to Kadroth, serving as a young gatekeeper/guard at Caer-Dineval castle - currently the only guard on rotation in the Guard Towers. Tricked by Glix's psychic communication into letting the party inside. Deliberately withheld his name from the party during the encounter, trying to avoid getting in trouble for letting them in - the party doesn't yet know his name.

title: Mama Chrys's Augury - Weal for the Spire Plan (Flux'thuun-Tinted)
description: Before leaving Lonelywood, Mama Chrys cast Augury to check whether heading to the Lost Spire was a sound move toward the party's ultimate goal of defeating the Rime (their own shorthand for ending Auril's winter/curse for good). Result: Weal. Notably, the casting was visibly influenced by Flux'thuun, which reframed the reading to emphasize ongoing movement/process over any single fixed destination - implying the 'correct path' may not strictly require reaching or completing the Spire as originally conceived, so much as continuing to act and move forward generally. Worth remembering as a hedge if the Spire plan needs to pivot or gets interrupted - the augury doesn't lock the party into that specific location being the answer.
